svg.text: B Standalone sub-mechanisms — six factory tricks, scaled down
Each panel loops on its own. These parts can be used in any concept (Fallturm, Trommelwerk, Kolbenstrang, Flachband or others).
source: B-process-line.md section 4
N2/N4 shown in B-flachband, N6/N17 in B-own-lid-dosing
N1 Buch-Wender (book flipper)
Two hinged leaves; closing the book turns what lay on leaf 1
onto leaf 2, upside down. Also breads both sides, flattens,
presses dough and patties; with two pans: a clamshell flip.
N3 Seam-down braising cassette
Rouladen are not tied: pushed seam-down into a plain sheet-metal
rack, the weight keeps the seam shut while they brown and braise.
The rack is washed as ware. Removes "tie the Roulade" entirely.
N8 Reversing-helix discharge

g.text: forward: charge stays at the back
reverse: helix screws it out ≈ 80 mL/rev

svg.text: A low internal spiral keeps the charge in one way and screws it
out of the mouth the other way: no door, no full tilt, and equal
portions by weight onto four plates (concrete mixer principle).
N9 Recipe water as chase
The liquid the recipe needs anyway is dosed last, through the
soiled path: it carries the last 1–3 % into the pot and leaves a
pre-rinsed surface. Better yield and accuracy; costs nothing.
N10 Thermal-shock peel in the drum
Heat the dry drum wall, tumble the wet potatoes, quench, then
rub with rubber studs: peel loss 6–10 % instead of 12–20 %,
smoother surface. Tomatoes and peaches skin the same way.
N11 Orbiting rounder cup
Bakery rounding: a 70 mm cup with a wet wall orbits over a wet
plate and rounds 60–150 g of dough or mince into a ball; a 40 %
squash gives a patty whose edges do not crack in the pan.
